\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevinAlgorithm.Resources}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Correctness of a query-state output]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b002
}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and
let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. A query state is a correct output if
there is a finite family $A$ of coordinate sets such that its active family is $A$,
every Fourier coefficient of $f$ with magnitude at least $\tau$ is indexed by a set in
$A$, every set in $A$ has Fourier coefficient magnitude greater than $\tau/2$, and $|A|$
is at most the active cap at threshold $\tau$ and at most $4/\tau^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Query budget]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryBudget}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryBudget}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. Define
the query budget as $n$ times twice the active cap at threshold $\tau$, times twice the
Fourier-estimator sample count at the weight-accuracy and call-confidence parameters
specified by $n$ and $\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Work budget]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinWorkBudget}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinWorkBudget}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. Define
the work budget as $n$ times the sum of the controller step-work bound and twice the
active cap at threshold $\tau$ times eight times one more than the Fourier-estimator
sample count, multiplied by $n+1$; the sample count uses the weight-accuracy and
call-confidence parameters specified by $n$ and $\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Active cap bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_cast_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\le 1$, and define $C=\left\lceil
4/\tau^2\right\rceil$. Then $C\le 8/\tau^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Active cap bound with an additive one]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_add_one_cast_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_add_one_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_cast_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\le 1$, and define $C=\left\lceil
4/\tau^2\right\rceil$. Then $C+1\le 9/\tau^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure-bit bound for call confidence]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence_failureBits_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence_failureBits_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every rational threshold $\tau$ with $0<\tau\le 1$, let
$A=\lceil 4/\tau^2\rceil$ and let $\delta=1/[40(n+1)(A+1)]$. Then
$\lceil\log_2(2/\delta)\rceil$ rounded up to the least power-of-two exponent, namely
$\operatorname{clog}_2(\lceil 2/\delta\rceil)$, is at most $80(n+1)(A+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin sample count bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinSampleCount_cast_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinSampleCount_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence_failureBits_le, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $0<\tau\le1$. The estimator sample count at accuracy
$\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter $1/[40(n+1)(\mathrm{cap}(\tau)+1)]$, where
$\mathrm{cap}(\tau)=\left\lceil4/\tau^2\right\rceil$, when regarded as a rational
number, is at most $5120(n+1)(\mathrm{cap}(\tau)+1)/\tau^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for the query budget]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryBudget_cast_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryBudget_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_add_one_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryBudget, FABL.goldreichLevinSampleCount_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and rational $0<\tau\le1$, let
$C=\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$, $\delta=1/[40(n+1)(C+1)]$,
$b=\lceil\log_2\lceil2/\delta\rceil\rceil$, and $m=\lceil2b/(\tau^2/4)^2\rceil$. The
Goldreich–Levin query budget $n\cdot 2C\cdot 2m$ is at most $2^{21}n(n+1)/\tau^8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin Work Budget Bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinWorkBudget_cast_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinWorkBudget_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_pos, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_add_one_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinSampleCount_cast_le, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy, FABL.goldreichLevinWorkBudget}
\difficulty{5}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every rational threshold $0<\tau\le1$, the
Goldreich–Levin work budget, viewed as a rational number, satisfies
$\operatorname{WorkBudget}(n,\tau)\le 2^{25}n(n+1)^2/\tau^8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin query program]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p089-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. The
query program is the membership-query learning program obtained by running the
Goldreich–Levin query procedure through $n$ stages at threshold $\tau$, and it returns a
state consisting of an optional active family of coordinate sets and a list of estimate
records.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $0<\tau\le1$ be a rational threshold. Every outcome in the support of the query
algorithm’s run with target $f$ uses at most $4n\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil m$ membership
queries, where $m=\left\lceil 2\,\mathrm{clog}_2\!\left(\left\lceil
80(n+1)(\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil+1)/\tau^2\right\rceil\right)/(\tau^4/16)\right\rceil$. Here
$\mathrm{clog}_2(r)$ is the least natural number $j$ such that $r\le2^j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness when no estimate fails]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_correct_of_mem_support_of_not_hasFailure}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_correct_of_mem_support_of_not_hasFailure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_card_le, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_complete, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_sound, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_satisfiesInvariant_of_mem_support}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $0<\tau\le1$.
For any outcome in the support of the Goldreich–Levin query program run against $f$, if
its estimate trace contains no inaccurate record (each record's estimate differs from
the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$), then the outcome's
state is correct: its active family exists, contains every $U$ with $\tau\le|\widehat
f(U)|$, contains only sets with $\tau/2<|\widehat f(U)|$, and has cardinality at most
both $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$ and $4/\tau^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Incorrectness is bounded by estimate failure]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_failureProbability}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_failureProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability_ne_top, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_correct_of_mem_support_of_not_hasFailure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $0<\tau\le1$.
The probability that the Goldreich–Levin query program produces a state that is not
correct is at most the probability that its estimate trace contains an estimate with
error at least $\tau^2/4$ from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure probability bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_failureProbability_le_one_twentieth}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_failureProbability_le_one_twentieth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinFailureBudget_rat_le_one_twentieth, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_outerFailureProbability_le, FABL.goldreichLevinStageFailureBudget}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $0<\tau\le1$.
The probability that the trace produced by the Goldreich–Levin query program contains an
estimate whose error from its corresponding restricted Fourier weight is at least
$\tau^2/4$ is at most $1/20$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin output failure bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_one_twentieth}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_one_twentieth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_failureProbability_le_one_twentieth, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_failureProbability}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $0<\tau\le 1$ be a rational threshold. Run the Goldreich–Levin query algorithm
with target $f$, and for each $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ write $\widehat f(U)=\mathbb
E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in U}x_i]$, where $x$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. The probability
that its output fails to be a state whose active set contains every $U$ with $|\widehat
f(U)|\ge\tau$, contains only sets $U$ with $|\widehat f(U)|>\tau/2$, and has cardinality
at most both $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$ and $4/\tau^2$, is at most $1/20$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin output failure bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_one_tenth}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_one_tenth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.IsCorrectOutput, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryProgram_incorrectProbability_le_one_twentieth}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:
\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $0<\tau\le 1$ be a rational
threshold. Run the Goldreich–Levin query algorithm with target $f$, and for each
$U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ write $\widehat f(U)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in U}x_i]$,
where $x$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. The probability that its output fails to be a
state whose active set contains every $U$ with $|\widehat f(U)|\ge\tau$, contains only
sets $U$ with $|\widehat f(U)|>\tau/2$, and has cardinality at most both
$\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$ and $4/\tau^2$, is at most $1/10$.
\end{theorem}
